text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 59 A gender-responsive grievance mechanism is a formal system or process that allows individuals, groups, or stakeholders (like employees, suppliers, or communities) to raise concerns about an organisations' activities or the activities of their employees and seek redress for any harm they have experienced. To be gender-responsive it should be designed to address complaints and seek redress that explicitly considers gender-based risks and inequalities. A well-designed gender-responsive grievance mechanism typically includes the following points: • Clear Channels: Defined ways to raise concerns (e.g., hotlines, emails, online platforms), • Gender Sensitivity: The mechanism should be aware of gender dynamics, including power imbalances and potential biases in the complaint process, • Anonymous Reporting: Mechanisms to allow individuals to report concerns without fear of retaliation (unless legally restricted), • Formal Procedures: Established processes for investigating complaints, assessing their validity, and determining appropriate remedies. Investigations should be conducted impartially and be sensitive to gender-specific concerns, • Protection from Reprisal: Individuals who lodge complaints must be protected from any negative consequences, • Redress Options: Potential solutions or actions to address the grievances, includi

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: ng access to justice/legal action, corrective actions, compensation or changes in company policies, • Gender Diversity: The mechanism's staff should reflect gender diversity, and they should be trained on gender sensitivity and unconscious bias, and • Monitoring and Evaluation: The mechanism's effectiveness should be regularly monitored and evaluated to ensure it provides equal access and outcomes This provides guidance for how to assess a gender responsive grievance mechanism. Not all elements are required; entities and investors are advised to ensure key elements such as Gender Sensitivity and Gender Diversity are present at a minimum. A gender-responsive grievance mechanism can be used to meet both the Management System requirement of Governance and Accountability and the GBVH requirement of Basic 2X ESG, at the investors discretion. title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: 1. Who should the investor/FI1 count as entrepreneursand owners? Under 1A: Ownership, women must either own at least 51% of the organisation. When counting ownership in the presence of institutional investors, the ownership must be traced to the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO). The percentage of ownership by women of the UBO can be counted as "women’s" shares. If the UBO cannot be traced, those shares should be counted as 0%. Under 1B: Entrepreneurship, at least 50% of the founders who retain an active role in the organisation must be women.2 A founder is any individual included in the legal registration of the organisation with a substantial decision-making role when the organisation was first established. Illustrative examples: Example: An investee was legally registered in 2010 with equal ownership between two women and a man. All three still have significant roles within the company and together have majority ownership: the women own 70% together and the man owns 30%. The investee is considered 2X aligned. Example: An investee was co-founded by a husband-and- wife team. Both the husband and wife retain an active role. The investee is 2X aligned because it has one woman founder. Example: An investee was legally registered in 2010 with equal ownership between two men and a woman as founders, i.e. each founder owns 1/3 of the shares. All three still have significant company ro

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: les and together have majority ownership. Since women founders are not at least half of all founders, Criteria 1 is not fulfilled. Example: An Ag-tech investee was launched in 2010 by two men who own the company,and on the same day, signed three women onto the pay roll, who are all now in senior leadership roles. Although the three women were present from day one, they do not count as founders nor owners and the company does not align with Criteria 1. 1 Investing in financial intermediaries that support women entrepreneurs is covered under the Criteria 6 (Portfolio). 2 See FAQ 2 in this section for clarification of what it means to retain an ‘Active Role’ in an organisation. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 63 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: An active role can refer to a key position in the organisation’s senior executive team (C-suite or equivalent). It may also include acting in an advisory capacity for key decisions and does not necessarily require a full-time role at the organisation. Considerations: Based on the specific context of the investee, different decisions could be considered as ‘key’ and different roles could be considered ‘active’. Investor/FI can consider parameters such as the following: • Clear decision-making authority, • Meaningful involvement in board or senior management meetings, • Serves as a strategic advisor, • Presence on company website or other communications materials (should be recent/prominent), and • Representation of the company externally (in activities with significant business impact) If a Founder leaves a company, they are no longer considered to have an active role and are not included in the calculation. She raises capital from investors, and as a result, her shareholding drops to 40%. Accordin

Example: A woman entrepreneur launched a company and has since sold her majority stake to a male-dominated private equity firm. She stepped back as CEO, and instead is seen as an expert voice on key topics relevant to the company’s decision-making process. However, she engages irregularly, when she is requested by the Board rather than at set times and her advice is sometimes disregarded when considering long-term strategic advice. The investee does not align with the 2X Criteria. 2. What constitutesa founder retainingan "active role" in a company?

If she sells the business entirely and does not remain involved in the company, the Criteria is not met. Shareholding can drop if investment is received but would still qualify through having a woman founder, Criteria 1B. Example: A tech startup is solo founded by a woman and she initially owns 100% of the company. She raises capital from investors, and as a result, her shareholding drops to 40%. According to the 2X Criteria, the company can still be counted as women-founded if she remains actively involved in the business, because over 50% of the founders are women (in this case 100%). Example: A tech startup is founded by a women, who retains 40% of the shareholding. text: The 2X Criteria Thresholds for Leadership and Employment are based on the latest benchmarking data at the nexus of country and sector (see the 2X Criteria thresholds). Sectors: When having to choose between multiple sectors, the investor/FI can choose to aim for the primary sector that the investment or use of proceeds maps to, or the one with the higher threshold, or a blend if it truly feels like it fits multiple sectors. Meanwhile, funds should be assessed for the Financial and Insurance Activities threshold (at the fund manager level). Countries: When having to choose between multiple countries, the investor/FI may choose between three approaches to determine which threshold to apply to the Leadership Criteria, based on what is most appropriate for the particular context: 1. Select the primary country that the investment or highest use of proceeds maps to, 2. Select the country with the higher threshold, or 3. Use the individual thresholds for each country where the investee operates. If using either approach 1 or approach 2, the leadership count should be in aggregate across all of the operating countries i.e leadership numbers from all countries should be aggregated and compared to the threshold that is highest among those countries. In the context of funds, the fund manager should be assessed based on the country where the fund manager's leadership team (Managing Partner

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: s and Partners) is based and employed (not where the fund is domiciled), whilst portfolio companies of funds should be assessed based on the primary country where their leadership are located. Each portfolio company will be assessed based on a threshold specific to their context. For companies who are headquartered in one country but operate and serve another, Leadership should be assessed where the headquarters are located. Example: An investor/FI is determining 2X alignment of a fund investing in the MENA region, established in Mauritius. The team has its office and a majority (75%) of their investments in Egypt. The investor/FI uses 2X Criteria thresholds for Financial Services in Egypt to determine 2X alignment at the fund manager level. Example: An investee provides educational content to new mothers via a cellphone application. Women comprise 35% of the company’s leadership team. The investee classified itself in the telecom sector, but the investor/FI decides it is more appropriate to map it to the education sector (higher threshold) and uses the higher threshold to assess alignment. The investor/FI determines it is not 2X aligned. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 73 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio C

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: When calculating the share of women in the workforce of companies and FIs, the investee must consider all employees types which may include any of the following depending on context: permanent, temporary, full-time, part-time, or contractors of either the entity or third- party agency. Under the Employment Criteria, informal workers are not counted. As employee types can vary, the quality indicator must be linked to the most representative employee type(s). The investor/FI can determine which employee type(s) are the most representative by considering their relative size. Types of employees comprising 30% or at least 100 people of the workforce should be counted. Moreover, the investee should have at least one workplace-focused effort ("one quality Employment indicator beyond compliance") to increase the share of women employees and/or to support them. Personnel that are included in the Leadership calculation are also considered to be employees and should be included in the employment calculation. This aligns to the methodology used to determine Employees under IRIS+ and applies to companies, FIs and funds. Illustrative examples: Example: A manufacturing firm relies on a large part-time seasonal contract staff to help process export forms during tax season. As both part- time seasonal and full-time employees are critical to the business’ operations (each representing ±1/3 of th

Women family members play a significant but informal role in picking the crops on the farms, but are not part of the contract scheme, and their pay/benefits are unclear. This is not 2X aligned. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 77 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix 1. title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: When calculating the share of women in the workforce in funds, the fund must consider all employees types which may include any of the following depending on context: permanent, temporary, full-time, part-time, contracted. Under the Employment Criteria, informal workers are not counted nor are third-party contracted workforce. For funds, typically the fund manager team dedicated to a particular fund (including leadership/partners) should be included within the total ‘count’ for employees. This includes non-investment employees who are dedicated fully or partially to the fund. They should be counted on a full time equivalent (FTE) basis. Investors can apply reasonable judgement to ensure the role is meaningful in this fund. This is especially important given that fund teams can be relatively small. In some cases, investors may apply discretion to assess Employees at the fund manager firm-wide level. Considerations when opting to use this approach are: • Investors should be able to justify why they are assessing the firm-wide employees. • Consideration should be given to how forward looking firm-wide gender targets are cascaded down to individual teams; and how these gender targets compare to actuals. • Whilst it is acceptable to count all employees across investment, impact/ESG, operational and administration roles, it’s important for investors to consider if concentrations of w

text: omen’s representation in non-investment and/or administration roles are skewing the figures. • The same approach should be taken for assessing the Leadership Criteria as taken for the Employment Criteria. Investors may refer to organograms and hiring plans to ascertain employee roles. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 78 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix 2. text: For Criteria 3 (Employment) to be met, there should be no dissonance with Criteria 2 (Leadership). Both indicators should be evaluated. To meet the minimum requirements for Employee diversity, there must be no dissonance between this and the Leadership Criteria, which means either the Senior Management, Board or Investment Committee. If the investee meets the variable threshold for employee diversity but has less than 10% women in Senior Management, Board or Investment Committee, it does not meet the minimum requirements for the Employment Criteria. The dissonance threshold applies to any of one the three components within Leadership: Senior Management, Boards or Investment Committee. To meet the minimum requirements under Employment where there is dissonance with Leadership, the investee must be willing to make a time-bound commitment to reaching at least 10% women in Leadership. This commitment operates like other Commitments whereby the investee must commit to achieving the indicated threshold within a reasonable timeframe as well as demonstrating progress within 2 years. This will be considered as commitment to a 2X Criteria, it is not considered as meeting the 2X Criteria. This means a second 2X Criteria will be required to be met in full. Illustrative examples: Example: A fund manager meets the Employment Criteria (threshold and quality indicator), There are no women as P

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: artners with investment-decision making authority, and no women on the Investment Committee. There is a dissonance with the Leadership Criteria. The fund manager makes a formal, time-bound commitment to reach a target of 30% women on the Investment Committee within 4 years, with interim progress demonstrated after 2 years. The investment qualifies. Example: A company meets the Employment Criteria (threshold and quality indicator), but has only 5% of women in Senior Management and 5% on the Board, i.e. there is a dissonance with the Leadership Criteria. The company is not willing to make a formal commitment to improve Leadership diversity,thus the dissonance cannot be resolved. The investment does not qualify. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 79 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix 3. text: The quality indicator addresses workplace-focused efforts to increase the share of women in the workforce and/or to support them. This builds on the original 2X Criteria’s focus on women’s recruitment, retention and career advancement. It includes efforts linked to any of the five categories below that address women’s barriers to quality employment: • Diversity efforts to increase the share of women in the workforce (e.g. recruitment practices to drive gender diversity; employee support practices including Employee Resource Groups) • Equal pay efforts to address any gender pay gap(s) identified • Equal care efforts to support employees with their care responsibilities (e.g. retention efforts that ensure an inclusive working environment for women employees with care responsibilities including paid parental leave, flexible working policies, etc.) • Health and wellbeing efforts to support the gender-specific health and wellbeing needs of employees • Efforts to address and prevent gender-based violence and harassment1 The following pages provide more examples on quality indicators an investee can consider under the Employment Criteria. Please note that these indicators must be above the legal minimum (i.e. beyond compliance), there must be evidence of implementation. The policies used to meet the Governance & Accountability requirements may be used to meet the Employment Quality In

text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 81 Examples of quality indicators: Diversity • Explicit, time-bound targets for the share of women in the workforce • Regular collection and analysis of gender-/sex-disaggregated data regarding the share of women in the workforce • Hiring efforts designed to eliminate bias and diversify talent pipeline, e.g. gender-balanced interview panels, anonymised resume screening, trainings for recruiters on unconscious bias) • Dedicated employee support with a gender focus, e.g. employee resource groups • Performance management/review process designed to eliminate gender bias • Training on unconscious bias and/or diversity, equity and inclusion Health and wellbeing • Efforts to address the gender-specific occupational health & safety (OH&S) needs of employees Examples: involvement of women in decision making, proactive management of gender-specific health and safety risks, physical workspace and facilities that address gender-specific needs of employees including among others toilet facilities and exposure to hazardous materials, support for pregnant and breastfeeding employees) • Employer-sponsored health insurance options Examples: cost coverage for gender-specific health services including among others: contraception, family planning, maternal health, menopausal health) • Other efforts or benefits regarding gender-specific health in

text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 84 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix The 2X Criteria Thresholds for Leadership and Employment are based on the latest benchmarking data at the nexus of country and sector (see the 2X Criteria thresholds here: 2xchallenge.org/2xcriteria). Sectors: When having to choose between multiple sectors, the investor/FI can choose to aim for the 'primary' sector that the investment maps to, or the one with the higher threshold, or a blend if it truly feels like it fits multiple sectors. Meanwhile, funds should be assessed for the Financial and Insurance threshold (at the fund manager level). Countries: When having to choose between multiple countries, the investor/FI can choose between three approaches to determine which threshold to apply to the Employment Criteria, based on what is most appropriate for the particular context: 1. Select the primary country that the investment or highest use of proceeds maps to, 2. Select the country with the higher threshold, or 3. Use the individual thresholds for each country where the investee operates. If using either approach 1 or approach 2, the employee count should be in aggregate across all of the operating countries

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: i.e employee numbers from all countries should be aggregated and compared to the threshold that is highest among those countries. In the context of funds, the fund manager should be assessed based on the country where the fund manager team is based and employed (not where the fund is domiciled), whilst portfolio companies of funds should be assessed based on the country of their operations. Each portfolio company will be assessed based on a threshold specific to their context. For companies who are headquartered in one country but operate and serve another, Employment should be assessed based on where the majority of full-time employees are based. Example: A fund manager is domiciled in Mauritius, the team is based in the UK and investing in East Africa. Since the team is based in the UK and employed there, the UK/financial services threshold should be used for the Leadership and Employment Criteria at the fund manager level. Example: An investee provides educational content to new mothers via a cellphone application. Women comprise 35% of the company’s leadership team. The investee classified itself in the telecom sector, but the investor/FI decides it is more appropriate to map it to the education sector (higher threshold) and uses the higher threshold to assess alignment. The investor/FI determines it is not 2X aligned. 5. How should the Employmentthresholdbe calculatedfor

text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 86 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix ThresholdCriteria Supply chains have traditionally been very opaque and gender- related issues have been pervasive but difficult to tackle given this opacity. The Supply Chain Criteria is designed to be qualitative rather than require a specific quantifiable metric, due to the nascent nature of assessing gender in supply chains and the difficulty in doing so. A strategic commitment asks that the entity makes a strategic commitment that demonstrates an explicit focus on women in the supply chain. This can be a public facing commitment or an internal commitment such as a policy or programme. A quality indicator applies to the strategic commitment to ensure that it will be implemented and as effective as possible. This may include ensuring there is a suitable process, action or detail in place to deliver upon the strategic commitment. Criteria detail: Threshold rationale: To be aligned with the Supply Chain Criteria, the investee must demonstrate: a. strategic commitment to women in the supply chain AND b. at least one “quality indicator” in the supply chain 1 Includes diversity practices, pay equity, care support,

What counts as strategic commitment/s under Criteria 4 (Supply Chain)? 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 88 Strategic support in place that demonstrate explicit commitment to women in the supply chain • Public commitment to women in the supply chain (e.g. gender-responsive procurement, gender equity in the supply chain, supporting women supply chain workers) • Compliance with written policy regarding women in the supply chain (e.g. gender-responsive procurement policy; policy regarding gender equity standards for suppliers) • Specific targets regarding women in the supply chain (e.g. procurement targets/goals for the amount and percentage spend with women-owned businesses; specific targets regarding gender equity in the supply chain) • Supplier diversity or inclusion code of conduct • Supplier diversity programme that includes women-owned/-led businesses • Strategy to increase the number of women-owned/-led suppliers • Actively seeks to source from suppliers that prioritise gender equity • Commitment to support women workers in supply chain companies, (e.g. a company has put in place programmes to support the upskilling of the supplier's workers) • Works with third party entity that verifies suppliers that are women-owned/-led The table below illustrates examples of how an investee can meet the strategic commitment this Criteria. The product or service must be material2 to the investees' revenue, sales volume or sales number. For each proposed 2X aligned investment, the investee needs to provide a rationale and clear links on how the product(s)/ service(s) offered are designed to be gender-responsive and have a direct positive effect on women/girls. Alignment with this Criteria can be further supported if the investee also demonstrates additional ways in which their product(s)/service(s) enhance the wellbeing of women/girls and/or drive gender equity. These can include the examples below (it is important to note that these are in addition to the primary requirement to enhance wellbeing, these are insufficient alone): 1. Product(s)/service(s) specifically target women customers 2. text: Example: A tech platform aggregates demand & supply of produce and provides logistics to move produce. 65% of its urban street vendor clients are women. The company commissioned a market study to understand how it could have a greater positive impact on women. Based on these insights, it applied a gender lens design to its product and measured that this is now saving women significant time contributing to alleviate their time poverty. Example: A tech platform aggregates demand & supply of produce and provides logistics to move produce. 65% of its urban street vendor clients are women. Based on these insights, it applied a gender lens design to its product and measured that this is now saving women significant time contributing to alleviate their time poverty. As this service is primarily used in locations with high rates of violence against women (5x global averages)1 and disproportionately benefits women, it is 2X aligned. text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 96 Investors should assess whether a significant proportion of the product(s)/service(s) that the investee offers enhance the wellbeing of women/girls i.e. that the Product/Service is material to the investees' business. Investor discretion can be used to determine what is material in the specific context of the investee. Investors should consider on what basis investees are able to calculate the proportion of the product(s)/service(s) that they offer that enhance the wellbeing of women/girls. A variety of approaches can be considered to serve as the basis for this judgement on materiality: Revenue or sales (USD or local currency equivalent) • What is the total revenue driven by all product(s)/ service(s) sold? • What is the total revenue driven by product(s)/ service(s) sold that enhance the wellbeing of women/girls? Volume of products/services sold (How many units of the product is sold) • What is the total volume of all product(s)/ service(s) sold? • What is the total volume of product(s)/ service(s) sold that enhance the wellbeing of women/girls? Number of products/services (How many products are offered) • What is the total number of product(s)/ service(s) that you offer? • What is the total number of product(s)/ service(s) that you offer that enhance the wellbeing of women/girls? There is no specific threshold for mater

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: iality that much be met. In some contexts, material may be deemed to be at least 50% of the investees revenue, sales, products sold or products offered. In contexts such as a large company with a larger product/service portfolio, or specific sectors with more limited gender considerations historically, a lower materiality proportion can be considered if reasonable explanation is provided by the investee whereby meaningful impact can be demonstrated. This guidance relates to products and services offered by companies. For funds with a GLI thesis and FIs offering financial products tailored to women, a determination of materiality is not required as it is considered that by meeting the Portfolio Criteria, the product or service would be deemed material. title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Investors using the 2X Criteria regularly conduct gender analysis alongside financial analysis. Gender analysis is an important part of building a product or service that enhances the wellbeing of women or girls or promotes gender equity. “A gender analysis examines the differences in women’s and men’s roles and responsibilities, daily routines and activities, and access to and control over resources, services and decision-making, including those that lead to social and economic inequalities.”1 What are some examples of gender analysis methodologies? Gender analysis may be conducted through various methodologies such as (but not limited to):2 • Sex-disaggregated surveys • Focus group discussions with women beneficiaries • Sex-disaggregated demand analysis which segments customer demand • Activity and incomes profiles, which help reveal how men and women spend their time and earn income • Access and control profiles, which focus on resources, asset ownership and access in households & community • Benefits profiles, which identify whose needs are likely to be met by the project services and facilities • Community mapping, which involves residents in mapping out assets and opportunities What is the difference between primary and secondary evidence? Primary evidence is data collected directly by the investee (e.g. focus groups). On the other hand, secondary evidence is data collect

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: ed by a credible and accurate external source (e.g. regional study by a statistics bureau). What determines if secondary evidence is relevant? The relevance of secondary evidence depends on three key dimensions: a. Geography: Data is focused on the local context of the project or is from a context which is similar enough for the insights to be transferable, b. Sector: Data is focused on the same sector as the project, and c. Date of collection: Data has been collected recently enough to be considered reliable in the current context 1 OECD, Handbook on the OECD-DAC Gender Equality Policy Marker, 2016 2 UNOPS, Guide on integrating gender throughout infrastructure project phases in Asia and the Pacific, 20192X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 97 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix 4. text: For projects which are designed – in part or as a whole – to respond to women’s needs, investees must: • Conduct gender analysis using primary evidence specific to the project (e.g. women focus groups, sex-disaggregated surveys or demand analysis) or relevant secondary evidence;1 and • Demonstrate a link between the gender analysis conducted/collected and the gender design features incorporated in the project. Illustrative examples: Example: A social housing project consulted secondary research and conducted focus groups to design the housing to address women’s stated needs, including safety (e.g. by locating waste collection bins in public, well-lit areas) and unpaid care responsibilities (e.g. by having all units overlook a communal playground where caregivers can oversee children from their unit’s window). Example: A sanitation project leads focus groups with a representative sample of local women to identify locations and designs for latrines which balance women’s needs for privacy with safety risks of isolation. Example: A highway is constructed in a region of Mexico. The investee wants to utilize secondary research in South Asia to justify the key adjustments made to the highway to design it for women’s unique needs. title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: A fund can meet Criteria 5 (Products & Services) if it has an intentional gender lens investment thesis. This counts as the fund manager meeting an institutional level Criteria, the Portfolio Criteria is still required to be met or committed to. A gender lens investment thesis requires the following to count: a. Gender is explicitly stated, and front and center in the fund’s investment thesis, and b. The fund pursues a gender lens investing strategy and gender is incorporated along the investment cycle. This includes gender being incorporated into investment decision-making structures and processes; assessing investments for opportunities to support gender equity along the 2X Criteria; supporting investees to realise these opportunities post-investment through targeted gender value creation; and tracking and reporting systematically on gender impact across the portfolio. We would generally expect a fund with a gender lens thesis to have gender incorporated across the entire investment lifecycle; however, as a minimum requirement, there needs to be evidence that gender is incorporated at least at certain stages of the investment cycle (such as e.g. origination or value creation). Best practice is that carry is partially linked to gender outcomes. With a gender lens investment thesis, it can be expected that the share of portfolio companies that are 2X aligned is at least as high

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: as the Portfolio Criteria threshold, meaning there is no dissonance with the Portfolio Criteria. Illustrative examples: Example: A fund focuses on supporting women entrepreneurs in South Asia, via a portfolio that includes direct equity stakes in women- led businesses and training services for aspiring entrepreneurs. The investment thesis states women’s economic empowerment as a strategic goal. This fund meets the Products & Services Criteria (explicit gender thesis and gender lens along the investment cycle) and the Portfolio Criteria. Example: A fund has an investment thesis explicitly focusing on the nexus of gender and climate. A gender lens is incorporated along the investment cycle, with a particular focus on gender action plans as part of the value creation strategy. This fund meets the Products & Services Criteria (explicit gender thesis and gender lens along the investment cycle). Example: A fund makes public statements about the importance of gender diversity. On its website and investor deck it speaks to its gender lens, however the investment thesis as such only mentions agriculture and climate. This funds does not meet the Products & Services Criteria, as gender isn’t front and center in the investment thesis. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 105 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepr

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: FIs can offer financial and non-financial products and services designed for women and fulfil Criteria 5 (Products & Services). For FIs, this can be financial or non-financial products designed for women. Examples include loans for women-led SMEs, banking or savings products for women's community groups, insurance products tailored for women. It is important that the product or service is designed to be tailored to women's needs and addressing the specific barriers or unserved needs they face. It may usetools such as needs analysis or market gaps as it pertains to women, affordability studies, women's focal groups. If an FI meets the Products and Services Criteria, this counts as the Direct Criteria. They are required to meet or commit tomeet the Portfolio Criteria. It is possible that the clients of the product or service which qualifies, form the clients counted underthe Portfolio Criteria. Where FIs lend to individual women, rather than companies, in the past this was assessed under Products & Services rather than under Portfolio. This current update to the Reference Guide has moved this to be included in the Portfolio Criteria, to facilitate understanding and when a FI has a hybrid portfolio of both client types. See more information. Illustrative examples: Example: An FI has created a dedicated lending line exclusive for women-owned SMEs. After conducting a comprehensive a

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: nalysis of the needs of women, they have designed their product with reduced collateral requirements and created loan incentives through interest reduction. Furthermore, the FI conducted community awareness and financial education campaigns directed at women borrowers and their households. Apart from this, the FI also has another lending facility that reaches 55% women. This FI meets both Criteria 5 and 6. Example: An insurance company serves a diverse customer base and offers a diverse product range. The company has developed tailored products for car insurance, which was developed through focus groups with women and include a specific focus on women’s needs. The product provides car insurance alongside recovery services and a commitment to women customers that they will be prioritised in the need of road-side response, and the support will arrive within 10 minutes in response to women’s safety needs. More than 50% of investor proceeds are allocated to this product. This insurance company meets Criteria 5. Example: An FI has created one specific lending line within their portfolio that aims to increase their women clients. This same product has reached 50% women. To qualify under Criteria 5, the FI must demonstrate how this lending line benefits women. Moreover, the same lending line cannot be used to qualify under Criteria 6, even if it targets 50% women clients because it wi

Financial Institutions (FIs) • Financial Institutors includes banks, MFIs, and non-bank financial institutions. • If lending to companies or other registered entities: Either the FI commits that 30% of the investor/FI loan proceeds will go towards businesses that meet one 2X Criteria or the FI's existing portfolio comprises at least 30% businesses (by volume or value) that meet one 2X Criteria. • If lending to Individuals: At least 50% of clients (by number) are women, women comprise 50% of total portfolio or 50% of investor proceeds going to women. • If an FI has a hybrid portfolio where they lend to both individual women and companies, this will be considered as two different portfolio segments and assessed separately. text: Financial Institutions (FIs) To be 2X aligned, FIs must meet the Basic 2X ESG,1 meet Governance & Accountability2 requirements, meet one Direct 2X Criteria and meet the Portfolio Criteria. Either the Direct Criteria or the Portfolio Criteria (not both) may be a time-bound commitment to meet the Criteria. Important Notes: • Criteria 6A: If use of proceeds is stipulated in a legal doc, the portfolio threshold counts as "met" not "commitment", • Portfolio Companies of FIs must meet one Criteria (i.e. no additional Criteria commitment, Basic 2X ESG, nor the Governance & Accountability metrics), • At the Portfolio level, FIs may use the country-sector specific thresholds or simplified thresholds (see this page), and • FIs can only qualify under the Supply Chain Criteria if they indeed have a significant supply chain. The following considerations may be applied: • If the FI lends to registered entities: It meets the Portfolio Criteria if 30% of the investor loan proceeds OR 30% of the FI’s portfolio must support businesses that meet one 2X Criteria. • If the FI lends to individuals, it meets the Portfolio Criteria if at least 50% of clients are women, women comprise 50% of total portfolio or 50% of investor proceeds going to women. • As FI portfolios are typically very granular with hundreds or even thousands of MSME clients, there is the option to use simplified thresholds for Leade

The threshold must be reasonable and an average for the main sectors represented in the portfolio. • The FI itself must meet at least one of the 2X Criteria 1-5 or make a time-bound commitment to doing so. Where FI meets the Employment Criteria, the investor should pay special attention to ensure there is no dissonance with the Leadership Criteria (i.e. that there are at least 10% women in Leadership). • If use of proceeds is stipulated in a legal document such as an ESAP, the portfolio threshold counts as "met" not "commitment”. 1 The FI does not need to screen all individual borrowers (or clients/customers) for gender risks. text: Illustrative examples: Example: An investor/FI invests in a fund with a clear target to have at least 50% of its portfolio in 2X aligned companies. The fund meets the Employment Criteria threshold but has no women at Partner level with decision- making authority or on the IC (i.e. there is dissonance between Employment and Leadership, women in leadership is below 10%). The fund manager makes a time-bound commitment to increase the women's representation on the IC to at least 10%. and develops a set of actions to get there. The investment can be considered 2X aligned. Example: An investor/FI invests in a financial institution which is considered an employer of choice for women in its country and meets the Leadership and Employment Criteria. The FI concludes that a 30% use of proceeds for WSMEs would be too aggressive given its challenging context. This investment is not 2X aligned unless the FI makes a commitment at the Portfolio level, either for the use of proceeds or for the portfolio as a whole. 1. text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 113 Below outlines a number of ways that an FI portfolio can be assessed. General loan to FI (no specific use of proceeds) At least 30% of its investment/financing must go to businesses who meet one 2X Criteria. Equity investment into FI that lends to companies At least 30% of the FI’s portfolio must go to businesses who meet one 2X Criteria. Equity investment into FI that lends to both individuals and companies If an FI has a hybrid portfolio where they lend to both individual women and SMEs, this will be considered as two different portfolio segments and assessed separately. text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 114 For an FI to be fully 2X aligned, it must meet one Direct Criteria along with meeting the Portfolio Criteria. One of these can be a commitment to meet the Criteria, but not both. Under the 2X Challenge, the full investment into the FI is counted. If an FI is unable to meet or commit to meet one Direct Criteria, a directed lending line provided to the FI is able to be 2X aligned even if the FI is not fully 2X aligned. Directed lending lines are defined as where a defined percentage of the financing is directed specifically to women individuals or companies who meet one 2X Criteria, and this is legally stipulated in a use of funds clause. It is important there is adequate governance to ensure delivery. Under the 2X Challenge, only the percentage of the financing that is stipulated to support women is counted. Use of proceeds commitments that are not specified in a legal document are not eligible to qualify as a Directed Lending Line. Equity Investments in MFIs/FIs do not qualify under directed lending rules. In equity investments, a FI must meet or commit to meeting one Direct Criteria at the institutional level alongside the Portfolio Criteria. text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 115 Double intermediated investments are less common, but examples can include an investor lending to a FI, who on-lends to a FI. The ability to monitor and set requirements for the end-beneficiaries of the finance is limited, especially for FIs. As such, simplified application of the 2X Criteria is acceptable. The rules are provided below and are presented from the view of the initial investor. A summary of this is provided on in the 2X Criteria Pathways. Investments into a FI that on-lends to a FI • The FI receiving the investor’s loan must meet Basic 2X ESG, Governance and Accountability, and one Direct Criteria. • The intermediated FI must meet the Portfolio Criteria. No Direct Criteria at the FI level is required. • To meet the Portfolio Criteria, the FI must meet or commit to meet 30% of its portfolio meeting one 2X Criteria using simplified thresholds. text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 118 Funds To be 2X aligned, funds must meet the Basic 2X ESG, meet Governance & Accountability requirements, meet one 2X Criteria at the fund manager level and meet the Portfolio Criteria. Either the Direct Criteria assessed at the level of the fund manager or the Portfolio Criteria may be a time-bound commitment to meet the Criteria, not both. The following considerations may be applied: • Funds typically attract investments before the start of the investment period and, by their very nature, certainly before thefund is fully invested. Therefore, the investor should agree to a portfolio level commitment aligned with the Portfolio Criteria. At the Portfolio level, either 30% of portfolio companies going into the fund or 50% at time of exit must meet one 2X Criteria. • It is possible that the fund manager seeks to be 2X aligned when the fund is fundraising and therefore has not begun disbursements, or the portfolio is not complete. As such, the fund can make a commitment to meet the Portfolio Criteria. If this commitment is bound in legal documents such as the limited partners agreement, this can be considered as met,enabling the institutional (fund manager) level Criteria to be a commitment. If this commitment is not legally binding, such as in a MoU, this is counted as a commitment and the Direct Criteria must be met in orde

This is typically investments into greenfield infrastructure, forestry, or real estate. See the complex structures chapter for more information. • Where fund managers meet the Employment Criteria, the investor should pay special attention to ensure there is no dissonance with the Leadership Criteria (i.e. that there are at least 10% women in Leadership). • Funds are aligned with the Products and Services Criteria if they have an intentional gender lens investing thesis. This requires that gender is explicitly stated in the investment thesis and a gender lens is incorporated along the investment cycle. See more here. • Note: The Supply Chain Criteria does not typically apply at the fund manager level, as fund managers typically don’t have significant supply chains. text: 7. For funds, what is the timing of 2X assessment in relation to the originationand exit of the fund? To meet the Portfolio Criteria, funds are required to have or commit that 30% of their portfolio meet one 2X Criteria at origination, or 50% at exit. If choosing to be 2X aligned at origination, i.e. at full deployment, portfolio companies of equity funds should be assessed on an individual basis at the time of the investment approval to determine if they meet one 2X Criteria. Data to undertake the assessment is typically collected at the due diligence stage. If the 2X assessment is undertaken more than a year before the point of investment, it should be reviewed to determine if it is still valid. This means the 2X assessment of portfolio companies within the same fund may be undertaken at different times in different years. The fund can be 2X aligned and qualify for the 2X Challenge before full deployment if there is a commitment to meet the Portfolio Criteria (30% at origination). The final determination of the 2X alignment of the Portfolio will be made at the end of the fund’s investment/disbursement period, when the fund is fully disbursed. This will be a once-off assessment. If it is found during monitoring that this was not reached, the fund would no longer be 2X aligned. If choosing to be 2X aligned at exit, the fund's portfolio is typically assessed at the end of the fu

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: nds' life, when all investments are exited. It is advised that this alternative timing of meeting the Portfolio Criteria is written into legal documents or an MOU so all parties are clear on the point at when the Portfolio 2X Criteria must be met (50% at exit). If the fund makes the 30% at origination or 50% at exit commitment in legal documents, such as the LP agreement of a Side Letter, the Portfolio Criteria is considered to be met. There must be a check at the end of the fund’s investment/disbursement period as per the guidance above to ensure this was attained. If the target is not attained, the fund is not 2X aligned. If the fund commits to the 30% or 50% requirement in a document that is not legal binding, such as a MOU, this is considered a commitment to the Portfolio Criteria. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 119 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix Example: A fund makes a legally binding commitment that 30% of the portfolio companies will meet one 2X Criteria at origination. The fund confirms 2X alignment of assessed portfolio companies during due diligence. The fund is considered to meet the Portfolio Criteria as a legally binding commitment has been made. text: Double intermediated investments are less common, but examples can include: • An investor investing into a fund of funds, or • An investor investing into a fund that invests in FIs In such cases, the ability to monitor and set requirements for the end-beneficiaries of the finance may be limited. As such, simplified application of the 2X Criteria is acceptable. The rules are provided below and are presented from the view of the initial investor. A summary of this is provided on in the 2X Critical Pathways. Investments into a fund of funds • The investee fund must meet Basic 2X ESG, Governance and Accountability and one Direct Criteria at the fund manager level. • The intermediated fund must meet the Portfolio Criteria. No Criteria at the fund manager level is required. • To meet the Portfolio Criteria, the intermediated fund must meet or commit to meet either 30% at origination or 50% at exit of portfolio companies meeting one 2X Criteria. Investments into a fund that invests in FIs • The investee fund must meet Basic 2X ESG, Governance and Accountability and one Direct Criteria. • The intermediated FI must meet the Portfolio Criteria. No Criteria at the FI level is required. • To meet the Portfolio Criteria, the intermediated FI must meet or commit to meet 30% of its portfolio meeting one 2X Criteria. 8. text: 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 121 The structure of real estate transactions often tends to straddle a ‘fund’ and a ‘complex structure’.Investors in real estate are likely to invest in a subsidiary of a listed real estate investment trust (REIT) or holding company, or directly into a real estate fund. In this guidance, these structures are collectively termed a 'real estate platform’. Whilst an SPV structured for an infrastructure investment typically has one underlying project, a real estate platform may invest into many assets, similar to a portfolio. As such, an investor should assess the real estate platform by applying the ‘complex structures’ guidance which allows for flexibility in the entity that is assessed and assess the underlying assets by applying the 'portfolio' guidance for funds. • Real estate platform/fund: Flexibility to assess at the sponsor or SPV levels which is equivalent to assessing at the ‘fund manager’ level. See the Complex Structures chapter for guidance on how to select which level is most appropriate to assess, noting that it may depend on the specific structure and scenario. • The assets are equivalent to a ‘portfolio’.Unlike typical private equity or venture capital funds, real estate funds tend to have limited influence over the tenants of the assets. Two scenarios for real estate investment platforms are expected: a. Singl

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: e asset real estate platform: If an investor is investing into a single asset real estate platform, then the investment can be evaluated as a company or complex structure (based on the type of transaction). b. Multi-asset real estate platform: If the real estate platform functions like an investment fund (i.e. channels money to multiple assets), the Sponsor or SPV should be assessed for a Direct Criteria (Criteria 1-5) and additionally the Portfolio Criteria must be assessed. The requirements are: o G&A and Basic 2X ESG at either Sponsor or SPV level, o Meet one 2X Criteria at the Sponsor or SPV level, and o Portfolio Commitment: 30% of assets to meet at least one 2X Criteria at origination or 50% at exit. text: Illustrative examples: Example: An investor provides capital to a SPV which will fund construction of multiple data centres. The SPV will be managed by the REIT’s team and will have the same IC as the REIT. All key decisions, including selection of assets will be approved by the REIT's management team. The investment is 2X aligned based on: • G&A and Basic 2X ESG are met at the REIT ('Sponsor' level) and is cascaded down to the SPV. • Meets Ownership Criteria at Sponsor level as the UBO of the REIT are women. • Commitment to ensure that the construction workers and employees of the assets meet the 2X employment thresholds. Example: An investor/FI invests in a holding company ‘platform’ that will establish a chain of hotel subsidiaries under one brand in various African countries. The platform sponsor meets the Leadership Criteria and commits to meet the Employment Criteria across the chain. This commitment is codified in the investment agreement and periodically monitored by the investor. The investment is 2X aligned. Example: An investor invests into an SPV which is managed and majority owned by a REIT. The SPV will develop greenfield and brownfield retail centers in peri-urban areas. G&A and Basic 2X ESG are met at the REIT (Sponsor level) and are cascaded down to the SPV. Leadership is assessed at the sponsor level and meets the required threshold. As a SPV with multiple und

text: Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Complex Structures Appendix 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 126 Complex Structures: Assessingalignment Investors often invest through intermediated structures that can make assessing 2X alignment challenging. These structures can include special purpose vehicles (SPVs), holding companies, project companies, trade finance, single asset real estate platforms, and others (for multi-asset real estate platforms including REITS, see Portfolio FAQ 8). These structures combined with additional related entities, including engineering, procurement and construction contractors, operations and management contracts, investorsand lenders, are collectively termed 'Complex Structures' for 2X Criteria purposes. Complex Structures can arise in any sector and are commonly seen in infrastructure investments into greenfield projects where SPVs are set up primarily for financial structuring purposes. Other common sectors include for investments in forestry and land-use and real estate. In such cases, assessing alignment to the 2X Criteria can be challenging, especially where the project company or project SPV within the Complex Structure is small and temporarily or thinly staffed. This chapter pr

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: The following pages provide more detailed guidance on how to select the most applicable assessment level for each 2X Criteria. Basic 2X ESG requirements • Basic 2X ESG must be met, commitments to meet this within 2 years via an Action Plan are permitted. • Assessment of Basic 2X ESG should be made at the level of the specific project SPV or project company within a Complex Structure. It is expected that the ESG practices of the sponsor are cascaded down to the project level. • The assessment should determine which entities are responsible for managing environmental and social risks, especially as it relates to safeguarding at the project level, and any possible exposure to environmental and social issues in the supply chain through an EPC contractor. Governance & Accountability requirements • Governance and Accountability requirements must be met, or a commitment made to meet them within 2 years. • For most cases, this should be assessed at the sponsor level, with consideration given to how Governance and Accountability measures are cascaded from a ‘corporate’ level down to the specific entities within the Complex Structure, if it is possible and relevant to do. • In the case of multiple sponsors, the lead sponsor with the largest share in the project SPV or project company should be the entity assessed for Governance and Accountability. • In some cases of smaller sponsors, Gov

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: ernance and Accountability measures may not be in place. It may make most sense for commitments to meet Governance and Accountability requirements to be developed ‘bottom-up’ from the specific project SPV or project company. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 129 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Complex Structures:Basic 2X ESG and G&A requirements Complex Structures

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Entrepreneurship & Ownership The Entrepreneurship and Ownership Criteria is typically not a relevant 2X Criteria in these transactions. As debt or equity investments are typically channelled into a project SPV or project company within the Complex Structure that are being set up for financial structuring reasons, there is no ‘Founder or Entrepreneur’ in the spirit of what is intended by this Criteria, and ownership will typically be held by institutional owners/investors as well as Sponsor companies themselves (as opposed to specific individuals). In cases where Entrepreneurship and Ownership of the project SPV or project company can be traced to individuals, it is possible to be 2X aligned through this Criteria. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 130 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Complex Structures:Entrepreneurship& Ownership Complex Structures

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Leadership The Leadership Criteria should be assessed based on investor discretion to determine women’s representation among relevant key decision makers. In some cases, key decision makers of a project may be most relevant to assess at the level of the sponsor. In such cases, consideration should be given to the relevant country used in the 2X Criteria Threshold Tool, as these decision makers may not be located in the country of the project itself. Further guidance on how to assess the Leadership Criteria in multiple geographies is available in FAQ 5. In other cases, the relevant entity within the project SPV or p roject company may have their own independent management team and/or independent board. In this scenario, women’s representation can be assessed within these decision-making bodies, assuming they are the key decision-makers. In instances where project SPV or project company board are not material or significant to the decisions of the project, investor discretion may be used to assess the board of the project sponsor. Employment The Employment Criteria should be assessed based on investor discretion to determine women’s representation among relevant 'employees'. This decision should take into account the size of the project SPV or project company , and where the majority of the employees who work on the project are based. For small SPVs with few full-time employees,

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: it may not be appropriate to count the employees officially employed or seconded to the SPV. In cases of large sponsors, counting all employees is not reflective of the individuals serving to operationalise the use of investor proceeds. It may be most relevant to count employees who are ‘seconded’ from these sponsors to work for project SPV or project company. Quality employment indicators, may, however, be assessed at sponsor level. In other cases, some the project SPV or project company may employ or contract individuals that are independent of the sponsor. In such cases, it is relevant to understand women’s representation among these individuals and the quality employment indicators at this same level to support the gender inclusion of these individuals. Contactors can be included in the employee count, if they are material to the operation of the project. See the Employment Chapter for more information on assessing contractors. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 131 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Complex Structures:Leadershipand Employment Complex Structures

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Supply chain The Supply Chain Criteria is typically assessed at the project SPV or project company level, as the decision-making entity over the supply chain used. In infrastructure projects, supply chain is often contractual based on different phases, e.g. Design, Construction or Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Investors often have limited leverage over the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) and/or O&M management which is typically selected by project sponsors, but it is at this EPC level of contracting where the Supply Chain Criteria and potential gender-inclusive approaches to procurement may be most relevant, e.g. commitments to work with a target number of woman-owned and -led subcontractors during the construction phase of a project. As such, in most cases it is most appropriate to assess the Supply Chain Criteria at the project SPV or project company. Products and Services To assess the Products and Services Criteria within a Complex Structure, it is recommended to refer to Products and Services FAQ 7-9 in the first instance. This covers Complex Structures that relate to infrastructure projects. It is recognised that this Criteria will not apply to all types of Complex Structures, or even all types of infrastructure transactions. For example, for utility-scale infrastructure projects where it is hard to robustly identify and quantify end beneficiaries, or e

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: vidence the expected enhanced wellbeing of women beneficiaries, this Criteria will not be applicable. Commitments Commitments to meet the Governance and Accountability and Basic 2X requirements or the 2X Criteria should be made by the entity that has the control, influence or decision-making authority on the particular 2X Criteria. This may be the sponsor, who would cascade the commitment to the SPV, the EPC contractor or the O&M contractor, or it may be the project SPV or project company,as the entity receiving the investment. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 132 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Complex Structures:Supply Chain and Products and Services Complex Structures

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Funds investing into complex structures are often funds focusing on investments into greenfield infrastructure, forestry, or real estate. For funds where at least 50% of the portfolio comprises investments into 'complex structures’, a lower threshold of 30% of investments meeting one 2X Criteria by exit can be applied. It is recognised that at the time of making a commitment to be 2X aligned, the composition of the fund portfolio may not be known, meaning the actual percentage of complex structure investments also may not be known. In these cases, the expected or anticipated level should be used, which should be based on and evidenced by the fund's investment strategy and/or the fund's policies and procedures. Previous fund vintages may also be used as an indicator, if relevant. There may be a range of fund strategies: some funds may focus only or predominantly on complex structure investments, and some may be mixed, with investments into companies alongside investments into complex structures. For a mixed portfolio, if 50% of the portfolio comprises investments into complex structures, the lower threshold of 30% by exit may apply. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 134 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendi

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Sponsors and the underlying project SPV or project company may be registered and/or operate in different countries. Selecting the appropriate country for the 2X Criteria thresholds for the Leadership and Employment Criteria is important. In such cases, investors should use their discretion to determine the country that is most appropriate in the specific context. For example: For the Leadership Criteria, if the majority of the decision makers for the particular project SPV or project company are at the sponsor level, and it is appropriate to assess leadership at the sponsor level, the country should be selected based on where the majority of these decision makers are located. This may be different to the location country of the project itself. It is important to guard against global leadership figures being used if those global leaders are not active decision makers on the particular project/investment under assessment. Often, leaders or management team members that are based in the region of the project are the primary decision makers. In other cases, project SPVs or project companies may have their own independent management teams and/or independent boards. The threshold should be determined based on where these management teams/boards are located. This may be in the project country. For the Employment Criteria, if assessing at the sponsor level, it is appropriate to select t

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: he country threshold where the majority of relevant employees are located. If assessing at the project company/project SPV level, in cases where the project SPV or project company employs individuals, which may include individuals who are independent of the sponsor, it is important to select the country where the majority of these individuals are located. This is often the country where the project is located. Example: An infrastructure company is based in Spain and established a SPV to develop energy infrastructure in Peru. The majority of the senior decision makers sit within the sponsor in Spain. Women’s representation among relevant decision makers exceeds 40%, the requirement for energy and power companies in Spain. The employees working directly on the energy project are based in Peru. Women’s representation among the SPV's employees exceeds the 25% threshold for Peru 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 135 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix 2. title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Guaranties and risk sharing facilities (collectively referred to hereafter as 'guaranties') are eligible to be 2X aligned. Guaranties are used for a broad range of purposes; for the 2X Criteria we focus on guaranties used to reduce or share the risk of loss on a specific transaction, project or portfolio of assets. These types of guaranties may be provided to a company, financial institution, fund or other entity. For guaranties provided to an FI, the guaranty may cover a portfolio of SME loans, trade loans, or a bond. Guaranties take many forms depending on the transaction structure and context. For the purposes of applying the 2X Criteria to investments and guaranties, we focus on five scenarios: 1. A guaranty provided to any entity or project company for a specific transaction or project 2. A guaranty provided to a financial institution (the Guaranty Holder) to guaranty a defined portfolio 3. A guaranty provided to a financial institution (the Guaranty Holder) to guaranty an undefined portfolio or a portfolio that cannot be assessed for 2X alignment at the time of the guaranty provision 4. A guaranty is provided to a third-party investor (Guaranty Holder) to cover the investor’s debt or equity investment in a financial institution. Use of proceeds from the debt/equity investment support lending to a defined or undefined portfolio 5. The provision of a guaranty alongside debt

text: to a financial institution (the Guaranty Holder) for a defined portfolio The following slides provide an overview of each scenario and the approach to apply the 2X Criteria, followed by a schematic of the structure of each scenario. Generally, we refer to financial institutions in the scenario guidance, however a similar approach can be applied to financial intermediaries more broadly, including funds. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 138 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Guarantiesand risk sharingfacilities Complex Structures

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Scenario 1: A guaranty provided to any entity or project company for a specific transaction or project This relates to guaranty coverage for a real sector project and may include a project company, similar to a SPV. If the guaranty is applied to a specific project which can be assessed for 2X alignment, the guaranty can be considered 2X aligned if the Guaranty Holder meets Governance and Accountability, Basic 2X ESG, one Direct 2X Criteria and the underlying guaranteed project is 2X aligned. The Complex Structures guidance may be useful in determining whether the project is 2X aligned. Scenario 2: A guaranty provided to a financial institution (the Guaranty Holder) to guaranty a defined portfolio This scenario applies when a guaranteed portfolio or the characteristics of a guaranteed portfolio can be defined at the time of the investment. This may include debt portfolios, directed lending lines, or trade loans. Under this scenario, the Guaranty Holder, i.e. the financial institution that receives the guaranty provided by the Guaranty Provider should meet: a. Basic 2X ESG requirements, b. Governance and Accountability requirements, c. one Direct 2X Criteria, and d. the portfolio of assets covered by the guaranty should meet the Portfolio Criteria (i.e. at least 30% of the potential portfolio meets one 2X Criteria). It is not required that the claims payment of the guaranty are t

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: racked in relation to the 2X alignment of the entities. Under the 2X Challenge, this transaction will be termed as a qualification of a 'Guaranty Facility' and 100% of the value of the coverage of the guaranty provision will be counted towards the 2X Challenge target. Under the 2X Challenge, if the Guaranty Holder does not meet or commit to meet a Direct 2X Criteria at the institutional level and/or the Governance and Accountability requirements, but the guaranteed portfolio of assets do meet the Portfolio Criteria, this is termed as the qualification of a 'Guaranty Portfolio' and is counted similarly to a directed lending line, where the percentage of the coverage of entities meeting one 2X Criteria is counted i.e. the value of the full guaranty is scaled down by the percentage of entities meeting one 2X Criteria (minimum 30%). 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 139 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Complex Structures Guarantiesand risk sharingfacilities

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Scenario 3: A guaranty provided to a financial institution (the Guaranty Holder) to guaranty an undefined portfolio or a portfolio that cannot be assessed for 2X alignment at the time of the guaranteed transaction In some cases, a guaranty provider will provide a guaranty to a Guaranty Holder (typically a financial institution) for a larger, less easily defined portfolio, such as a bank’s SME loan book, a FI's balance sheet, or a trade finance programme. In these cases, the portfolio will evolve, and it is difficult to define at any point in time. This makes it difficult to assess its alignment with the Portfolio Criteria. In this scenario, there are two options to 2X alignment - 3.1 Assess whether the portfolio has been tailored to encourage lending to women or 2X-qualifying businesses. A guaranteed portfolio that cannot be clearly defined or assessed for 2X alignment at the time of the transaction may still be 2X aligned if it has in place financial incentives or tailored its products to support 2X aligned entities. The financial incentives used may vary, but could include: • providing a lower cost of capital to 2X aligned entities, • providing a higher risk limit for 2X aligned entities, • providing a pricing discount or lower cost of capital to 2X aligned businesses, or • other incentives or schemes that encourage lending to 2X aligned entities.1 3.2 Assess the actual guara

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: nteed portfolio at the time of reporting. The portfolio may be considered 2X aligned if, in annual or biennial reporting, the financial intermediary demonstrates that at least 30% of the actual guaranteed portfolio are entities that meet one 2X Criteria. To ensure that adequate reporting, it is best practice that systems to provide gender-disaggregated data are established at the beginning of the investment/guaranty and/or included in the legal documentation. Note: for 2X Challenge investors, this qualification would occur at the time of the reporting, rather than the time of the investment. 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 140 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Guarantiesand risk sharingfacilities Complex Structures 1 If the tailoring or incentives are legally documented, the portfolio threshold counts as “met” not a “commitment”, allowing t he Direct Criteria to be a commitment.

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: Scenario 4: Guaranty covers a third-party investor’s (Guaranty Holder) debt or equity in a financial institution. Use of proceeds from the debt/equity investment support lending to a defined or undefined portfolio. Under this scenario, a Guarantor provides a guaranty to a third-party investor, who provides debt or equity to a financial institution. Often this is undertaken to reduce the risk borne by the third-party investor making the loan to the financial institution. The guidance under Scenario 2 and 3 can be applied in this instance. This means that the third-party investor (Guaranty Holder) must meet Basic 2X ESG and Governance and Accountability requirements, one Direct 2X Criteria, and the portfolio of loans originated using the proceeds from the third-party investment should also meet the Portfolio Criteria (i.e. at least 30% of the potential portfolio should meet one 2X Criteria). Scenario 5: The provision of a guaranty alongside debt to a Financial institution (the Guaranty Holder) for a defined portfolio In some cases, an entity may provide debt or a directed lending line to a financial institution and provide a guaranty on that same portfolio. This can be to guaranty: 5.1 The downstream loans of the financial institution (the Guaranty Holder), which is deploying the debt or directed lending line. In such cases, it is possible that both the debt and the guaranty is 2

title: 2025 OECD 2025-2X-Criteria-Reference-Guide-vF-1
text: X aligned. In these cases, they will both be 2X aligned, and they may both be qualified under the 2X Challenge.1 5.2 A loan from a third-party lender (the Guaranty Holder) into the financial institution receiving the debt. This is similar to Scenario 4, the addition being that the guarantor also makes a loan to the financial intermediary. In this scenario, the guaranty can be 2X aligned if the co-investor/co-guarantor receiving the guaranty and the underlying debt portfolio is 2X aligned . They may be qualified under the 2X Challenge.1 2X Criteria Reference Guide (Updated September 2025) 141 Content Overview How to use Principles 2X Criteria Basic 2X ESG Governance & Accountability Entrepreneurship & Ownership Leadership Employment Supply Chain Products & Services Portfolio Appendix Complex Structures Guarantiesand risk sharingfacilities 1 While both are eligible to be qualified under the 2X Challenge, the volume counted towards the 2X Challenge targets would be reduced to avoid any double counting these overlapping transactions.
